newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss plan two new mobile phone licenses.
newsitem.headline: Swiss plan two new mobile phone licenses.

text.p: Swiss authorities on Thursday proposed opening up the country's mobile telephone network to two new service providers in addition to Swiss Telecom as part of the liberalisation of the telecommunications market.
Federal communications office Bakom said in a statement the two licenses could first be awarded when a new law governing the Swiss telecommunications market takes effect in 1998.
Bakom, part of the Transport and Energy Ministry, will later decide on the date for a public tender.

State-owned Swiss Telecom, currently the sole provider of mobile telephone services in Switzerland, will maintain its license and said in a separate statement that it welcomed the opening of the market.

There are currently 500,000 users of the digital GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) system in Switzerland, known as Natel D, and 260,000 subscribers to the analogue network, known as Natel C.
One of the new licenses will be cover both the GSM and the DCS networks (Digital Cellular System).
A second license will only be awarded for the DCS standard due to the lack of available frequencies.
However, after January 1, 2001, the holder of the DCS license will also be able to provide GSM services and all three license holders will be treated equally, Bakom said.
DCS systems are currently only operating in Geneva under the name of Natel City. DCS networks operate outside Switzerland.
GSM and DCS systems are technically closely related and a future generation of mobile phones that soon will be on the market will operate with both standards.
Opening up the market to new competitors will require some changes to the mobile frequencies used by Swiss Telecom.
Swiss Telecom currently uses important parts of the analogue and the digital GSM frequency in Switzerland and to make room for new providers it has to rework some of its networks.
To ensure there are not interruptions to current mobile phone users, Swiss Telecom will continue to operate the analogue Natel C network until December 31, 2000, Bakom said.
